plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and a big flower head made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc packed with tiny florets that develop into seeds. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky. It is grown as a garden ornamental and a major oilseed crop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and Europe
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west during the day (heliotropism), but mature flowers stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Hydrangea paniculata
plants.description: A hardy deciduous shrub that produces large cone-shaped flower clusters. The blooms open creamy white and often age to pink or burgundy as late summer progresses, giving a changing display well into autumn.
plants.location: Native to China, Japan, and Sakhalin; widely grown in temperate gardens in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Unlike bigleaf hydrangeas, panicle hydrangeas bloom on new wood, so they reliably flower even after harsh winters, and their color does not depend on soil pH.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower of meadows, roadsides, and field edges, bearing dense plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects preparing for autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: Native to northern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, a bowl-shaped bloom of pointed pink bracts surrounding a center of pale, downy flowers. It thrives in the fynbos habitat on nutrient-poor, well-drained soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (peak around August to November, with some flowering through the year)
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the plant has adapted to wildfires with thick underground stems that resprout after burns.
